name: Switch
description: The APG switch: an on/off control drawn as a track and a thumb.

props.name: name
props.description: What the switch submits under. Needed for a form; a controlled switch can do without one.

props.name: props
props.description: Attributes for the `<input>` itself. `type` is the component's, and `role` is already `switch`.

props.name: onInput
props.description: Fires on every keystroke or click. On a checkbox this is the same moment as `onChange`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires when the switch is toggled. `e.target.checked` is the new state.

props.name: value
props.description: The value the form submits when it is on. Defaults to `"on"`, as HTML does.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focus it on mount. One per page at most — a stolen focus is a lost place in the document.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Rendered and read, but not toggleable. Unlike `disabled` it stays in the tab order and submits.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: The state it starts in when the switch is uncontrolled. Pass `checked` instead to control it.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the switch, rendered inside a label that wraps the input.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Styles for the wrapping `<label>`: the row's layout, not the track's own appearance.

keyboard.action: Focuses the switch. It is one tab stop, like any other control.
Toggles it. The platform supplies this one.
Toggles it too, and does not submit the surrounding form. APG lists Enter as optional, and a bare checkbox ignores it.

a11y: A real `<input type="checkbox">` under `role="switch"`, so focus, the disabled state and form submission are the platform's rather than this component's.
`aria-checked` is the input's own checked state — there is no second element to keep in step with it, and no mixed state to get wrong.
`label` renders the `<label>` wrapping the input, which is what names it. The track and the thumb are one element and its `::before`, so nothing decorative reaches the accessibility tree.
